text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein calls for continuation of work for a comprehensive Middle East peace.
- "Unity Dam" on Yarmuk River ready for implementation. Four year project would cost $213 million at 1988 prices.
- Development council met on Friday to discuss proposed amendments to law on companies.
- Amman branch of engineering union decides to go strike on November 20 to protest lack of response to their demands.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti and World Bank director general of Middle East and North Africa Inder Sud met on Friday to review Jordan's economic restructuring programme.
- Big fire in Zarqa after five fuel tankers collide.
- Telecommunications Corporation director general Walid el-Dweik says new phone tariff under consideration for 1997 would cut cost of international calls by 20 pct.
- Head of U.S. Central Command, Lieutenant General Binford Peay, arrived in Jordan on Friday for official visit.
